research_scope: Source-free context-complete mathematical equivalence review of common prerequisites; original candidate identities and the source wording are retained.

aliases.reason: The geometrically-integral source uses K equal to an algebraic closure of k, a special field extension; the geometrically-regular source describes the general extension-of-scalars K-algebra A⊗_k K. The underlying commutative unital k-algebra scalar-extension construction is identical, with chosen K preserved by source text.

The geometrically-reduced source specializes K to perfect closure k^perf; that is an extra field choice within the same general K-algebra scalar extension A⊗_k K used by the geometrically-regular source. The perfect-closure test is not replaced by an arbitrary-extension assertion.

The geometrically-connected source forms A⊗_k K with the canonical unital K-algebra multiplication and structure map. This is the same scalar-extension prerequisite as the geometrically-regular source, with connectedness of Spec(A⊗_k K) an additional requirement.

The matrix-rank source uses free modules R^m and R^n of finite ranks. The finite-presentation source provides the general finite-rank free module R^n notion, with rank variable and basis; this is the same prerequisite, not arbitrary projectivity.

Lazard's characterization states a filtered colimit of finite-rank free R-modules. These are instances of the R^n finite-rank free module used in the finite-module presentation sources; filtered colimit is an additional construction, not part of the prerequisite.
